items.title: Iran says its plan to end the war with the US could be implemented in under a week
items.summary: Business Standard reports Iran is continuing talks with intermediaries on a proposal to end the war, and foreign minister Araghchi said it could be implemented in even less than a week. Fox News' 28 October live coverage has Trump saying 'anything's possible' on strikes after the 3 November midterms, while CBS says he promised not to resume strikes before them. Reports conflict on the ceasefire's status, so treat this as provisional.
items.why: Gulf diplomacy drives oil prices and risk appetite, which shape corporate hiring and marketing budgets.
items.src: Business Standard, Fox News, CBS News

items.title: Ceasefire in a southern Ukrainian city holds as Moscow and Kyiv await US-led talks
items.summary: The Washington Times (28 October) reports a planned six-day ceasefire in and around a Russia-occupied southern city held through its first day and night, though fighting continued elsewhere. US-led plans to bring Moscow and Kyiv back for technical talks next month were reported, with no firm date. Details are early and provisional.
items.why: Progress on Ukraine affects energy and sanctions, which global employers plan around.

items.title: Inflation is near a two-year high after the RBI's October rate hike
items.summary: No dated India story from the last three days turned up, so this is three weeks old context. CNBC reported on 7 October that the RBI raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, its first hike since 2023. One search-summarised report puts September inflation at 5.5%, driven by food and fuel, while another cites 4.8% for August, so the latest figure is provisional; check the RBI's release.
items.why: Higher rates and prices raise company costs and can slow campus hiring and consumer spending.

items.title: Sensex and Nifty rebound after the US Fed holds rates steady
items.summary: ChiniMandi reports the Sensex rose 905 points to 74,151.04 and the Nifty gained about 1.05% to 22,936.75 on 29 October after the Fed paused, ending a run in which both had lost about 2% over seven sessions on high crude. Business Recorder also ties the gains to earnings. Index gain percentages differ slightly between reports, so treat them as provisional.
items.why: Market swings change campus-hiring sentiment and the risk appetite of recruiting companies.

items.title: Nifty closed at 22,936.75 and Sensex at 74,151.04 on 29 October
items.summary: Closing levels from the ChiniMandi report on the Fed-driven rebound; a single source, so provisional.
items.why: Useful reference levels when reading market commentary this week.

items.title: Anthropic files for a Nasdaq IPO, with security disclosures in the filing
items.summary: Search reports say Anthropic filed its IPO registration on 26 October to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, citing about $16.3 billion in first-half revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss driven largely by noncash charges. Fox News' 27 October live blog says the filing also discloses security incidents and a training pause. Figures come from secondary summaries and are provisional.
items.why: AI governance, disclosure and valuation are becoming central to how firms recruit and brand themselves.

items.title: Microsoft books about $10 billion from OpenAI arrangements in the quarter
items.summary: Implicator reports Microsoft's latest 10-Q shows OpenAI-related arrangements generated about $10 billion in revenue in the quarter to 30 September, alongside Alphabet's cloud growth. Separately, Tech Startups' 27 October roundup says Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to roughly 60,000 employees. These are secondary reports and provisional.
items.why: Workforce shifts at this scale reshape talent supply and the skills employers want.

items.title: Microsoft is reportedly offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
items.summary: Tech Startups' 27 October roundup reports the offer covers more than a quarter of Microsoft's global workforce. An aggregator report, so provisional.
items.why: A large HR event that signals how AI spending is changing workforce planning.
